mapping.name: STEP1-POSTGRES: connects to the real development PostgreSQL
STEP6-POSTGRES: real models survive reopen; version guards serialize competing edits; Nest exposes durable reads
STEP7-API-SIGKILL-before-commit: an actual API process crash preserves immutable wire, cursor and exactly one final operation
STEP7-API-SIGKILL-after-commit: an actual API process crash preserves immutable wire, cursor and exactly one final operation
STEP7-CLIENT-HTTP: offline Task/Relation chains survive SIGKILL and converge through restore/pull/push/pull in creation order
STEP7-CLIENT-ACK-LOSS: commit followed by dropped HTTP ACK and API/store restart is recovered once through durable pull
STEP7-CLIENT-CONFLICT: actual HTTP plus Rust stores preserve peer fields, expose both values, and converge after explicit new resolution
STEP7-CLIENT-PULL-FAILURE: cursor commit failure stops network progress; restart and explicit retry keep the original cursor and restore all records
STEP7-CLIENT-LATENCY: 500ms, 2s and 5s HTTP ACK delays never report pending edits as synced; repeated pause/resume keeps intent
STEP7-CLIENT-REJECTED: create collision stops the affected causal chain, retains both original payloads and never displays synced
STEP7-SERVER-IDEMPOTENCY: concurrent replays, ID collisions, malformed payloads and API recreation retain immutable results
STEP7-SERVER-MERGE: field merge keeps peer edits and same-field conflicts retain base/local/remote through explicit resolution
STEP7-SERVER-RELATION: disjoint endpoint edits merge and same endpoint conflicts resolve as a new operation
STEP7-SERVER-DELETE: deletes dominate stale Task/Relation updates and close existing conflicts without resurrecting entities
STEP7-SERVER-ORDER: concurrent writers cannot leave lower committed operations behind a pull cursor
STEP7-SERVER-ATOMIC: ledger failure rolls back entity/history/counter and retry finalizes exactly once
STEP7-SERVER-MIGRATION: Step 6 rows and tombstones enter the new stream atomically without fabricating missing history
STEP7-SERVER-CAUSAL: sequential offline intent keeps competing peer values and merges its own accepted fields
STEP7-SERVER-CAUSAL-VALIDATION: aliases preserve original intent, invalid dependencies reject durably and chained deletes remain acknowledged
STEP7-SERVER-CAUSAL-MIGRATION: existing version 2 ledger frames are reconstructed without changing immutable ACKs or cursors
